canonical_answers: Independent variable: object distance. Dependent variable: measured image distance or magnification. Control: focal length held fixed.

payload.text: A converging lens has focal length 0.200 m and an object is 0.600 m from the lens.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Design a feasible measurement that tests the governing relation; identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and one control.

criteria.description: A feasible measurement design: place the object at several distances from the lens and locate the sharp image on a screen at each position. Independent variable = object distance do; dependent variable = measured image distance di (or magnification); control = the lens's focal length (0.200 m), held fixed across trials.
required_evidence: dependent variable: measured image distance or magnification
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why assuming the lens thickness is negligible compared to the object and image distances justifies applying the thin-lens equation directly rather than a thick-lens model.

criteria.description: Explain why assuming the lens thickness is negligible compared to the object and image distances justifies applying the thin-lens equation directly rather than a thick-lens model.
required_evidence: thin-lens equation applies to the given distances
